data.body:
`make sanity` fails non-deterministically on unrelated changes because two
tests mutate process-global `PATH` while the rest of the suite runs in
parallel.

`src/installed_workflows/tests_registry_ext.rs:43,50,274,287` call
`std::env::set_var("PATH", ...)`. The two loom tests serialize against each
other through `env_lock` (`src/installed_workflows/tests_helpers.rs:102`) but
not against the other ~1280 tests, and `Command::spawn` reads `PATH` from the
process environment. When the race is lost,
`loom_failures_and_invalid_utf8_reported` fails its assertion at line 278, then
poisons `env_lock` and cascades into `read_bundle_source_can_shell_out_to_loom`
failing with `PoisonError`.

This is pre-existing, not a regression. It was reproduced at commit b693169e
(before the lease-owner and push-unblock work) by exporting the tree with
`git archive` and running `cargo test --bin knots` 13 times: 11 clean, 1 run
with 1 failure, 1 run with 2 failures. Running the module alone always passes.

`make sanity` is a required pre-push gate (CLAUDE.md), so this flake blocks
unrelated work and trains people to re-run until green.

Likely fixes, in preference order:
- Remove the `PATH` mutation: give the code under test an injectable lookup
  seam so the test passes an explicit binary path, the way `resolve_machine_id`
  takes its env value as a parameter (`src/machine.rs`).
- Failing that, run the affected tests in a child process with its own
  environment, so no global state is shared.
- A wider `env_lock` is not sufficient on its own: it would have to be taken by
  every test that spawns a process, which is not enforceable.

There is a related smaller case: `src/machine_tests.rs:90`
(`machine_id_reads_the_process_environment`) reads the real environment and
fails whenever the documented `KNOTS_MACHINE_ID` override is set
(docs/leases.md). Fix it in the same pass by using the injected-env seam the
other tests in that file already use.
data.title: Remove PATH mutation from loom tests that makes make sanity flaky
